source: Kansas Department of Health and Environment, Office of Vital Statistics, Annual Summary of Vital Statistics, county table 'Selected Causes of Death by County of Residence' (reports for 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024; PDFs saved 2026-10-10 from the department's document center)
url: https://www.coronavirus.kdheks.gov/DocumentCenter/ (Annual Summary of Vital Statistics full-report PDFs; per-file addresses in sources/ks_kdhe/SOURCES.tsv)
note: Annual county-by-cause table (Selected Causes of Death by County of Residence; Table 53-73 in the 2001-2013 reports, E27 from 2015) from the Kansas Annual Summary of Vital Statistics, 23 reports: 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024. 2016 is left out here because the same table is already staged from the Table D25 workbook (ks_kdhe_d25), and the two agree on all 1,470 cells compared. The 2020 and 2023 editions were found later on the department's year pages and added (2020 pages read with pdftotext -layout, because the text reader split some numbers such as 17 into '1 7'; scripts/ks_dump_extra.py, ks_build_extra.py). Each report prints 105 counties plus the Kansas row (and, from 2010, a not-stated row; from 2013, five peer-group rows that are not used). Counts are exact and zeros print as 0; the tables carry no suppression marks. Read by a script (scripts/ks_parse.py, ks_parse2001.py) from the saved PDFs, not typed. Checks run on every county row of every year: (1) the report's own arithmetic, where cancer = its seven site columns, heart = its four heart columns, and major cardiovascular disease = heart + stroke + atherosclerosis + other arteries + hypertensive renal disease, all hold in 100% of rows; (2) in every year the 105 county columns add up to the Kansas row for each of the 37 columns, except the 'all other causes' column in 2008 and 2009, which is 22 short in the county rows (Marion 6, Marshall 16, same in 2010) and is not used; (3) the all-causes column equals the sum of the cause columns in every row except 2008-2010 Marion and Marshall (the all-other column above) and about 1-2 rows per year in 2014, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2024 where it differs by 1 or 2 deaths because some cause groups overlap; all-deaths and the 12 map causes are as printed. In 2020 the all-causes column is 1 or 2 below the cause columns in Leavenworth, Sedgwick, Shawnee and Wyandotte and 1 above in Hamilton, while the not-stated row has 7 all-cause deaths but 3 in cause columns (four not-stated deaths seem to have been given a county in the cause columns only). The 2020 report reorganised its cause tables to include COVID-19 (per the 2024 report); this county table has no COVID-19 column, so those deaths sit in the residual groups and the column names used here are unchanged. Causes: all = All Causes; cancer = Malignant Neoplasms (all sites); heart = Diseases of Heart (CDC heart I00-I09, I11, I13, I20-I51); stroke = Cerebrovascular Diseases; Alzheimer's; diabetes mellitus; flu_pneumonia = Pneumonia and Influenza; clrd = Chronic Lower Respiratory Diseases; liver = Chronic Liver Disease and Cirrhosis (K70, K73-K74); kidney = Nephritis, Nephrotic Syndrome and Nephrosis; suicide; homicide. Suicide and homicide columns in 2009 and a few other years add terrorism codes (U01-U03); none are expected in Kansas counts. Kept raw: hypertension (hypertensive renal disease and secondary hypertension) and accidents (motor vehicle plus all other accidents and adverse effects; no map measure). Falls and overdose are not separate columns. A later check against CDC decides which years and causes the map may use. Terms: the reports carry no copyright, citation or reuse wording in their text; KDHE is the publisher (terms status none_stated). Counts only.
